title: Thresholded polynomial-time approximation
statement: For every real $\\eta>0$, there is a polynomial-time computable map $A$ from bit strings to bit strings and there are natural numbers $C,k$ with the following property. Whenever a bit string parses as a nonempty list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers, form the weighted graph that assigns each ordered pair $(u,v)$ weight equal to the total number of occurrences of $(u,v)$ and $(v,u)$ in $E$, divided by twice the length of $E$. For every angle $\\theta$ between the Goemans–Williamson angle and $\\pi$, inclusive, such that $(1-\\cos\\theta)/2$ is at most this graph’s SDP optimum, the expected cut value of the graph under the Boolean assignment given by the $v$th output bit of $A$ on the encoding of the input paired with a uniformly random bit string of length $C(\\lvert\\text{bits}\\rvert+1)^k$ (using false if the output has no $v$th bit) is at least $\\theta/\\pi-\\eta$.
hypotheses_covered: The bit string parses to the specified edge list
$\\theta$ lies in the closed interval from the Goemans–Williamson angle to $\\pi$
$(1-\\cos\\theta)/2$ is at most the graph’s SDP optimum
The random bit string has length $C(\\lvert\\text{bits}\\rvert+1)^k$ and is sampled uniformly
